solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lead errant fathers to turn over a new leaf

parts.note: the lead in a play or film is its star

indicators.note: errant means wandering or straying, so the letters of the next word stray out of order

explanation.surface: A headline-style plea for wayward dads to mend their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as a verb urging fathers on, but it is the noun: the leading role in a show. 'errant' makes TAFRESH.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning over a new leaf is an idiom for beginning again with a clean slate.

clue.text: Removed forcibly by wind, without further ado

indicators.note: without means minus, so the following word is taken away from the other piece

parts.note: a tornado is a violent whirling wind

explanation.surface: Something ripped off by a gale, promptly and without fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without further ado' looks like a stock phrase meaning promptly; here it takes ADO out of TORNADO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something torn from its place has been ripped away by force.

clue.text: Is sorry to announce hoax

indicators.note: announcing is saying out loud, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a ruse is a trick or hoax

explanation.surface: Someone regrets having to declare that something was a hoax.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to regret it, so one who rues feels regret.

clue.text: Apart from star, dear, twinkling outside

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go outside the other piece
twinkling suggests flickering movement, so these letters are shuffled

parts.note: the sun is a star

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme picture of a twinkling star, separated from someone dear.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls 'Twinkle, twinkle, little star'; 'twinkling' makes ADER, which 'outside' places around the star.
explanation.definitionFit: Split into pieces or separated, so torn into parts.

clue.text: Fashion of mid-Edwardian era

indicators.note: mid means the middle, so only the central letter of the word is used

parts.note: an era is an age

explanation.surface: A style from the middle of the Edwardian period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid' takes R, the central letter of the nine in EDWARDIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A craze or passing trend is all the rage, so the word means the fashion of the moment.

clue.text: Clumsily rib Irishman about being a foreigner

indicators.note: about means round, so the name goes round the other piece

parts.note: Sean is a typical Irish man's name

indicators.note: done clumsily means done awkwardly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone awkwardly teases an Irishman for being foreign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rib' looks like the verb tease, but it is anagram fodder: 'Clumsily' makes RBI, and 'about' wraps the Irish name around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Serbia, in the Balkans, is a foreign national from a British point of view.

clue.text: Hence this crossword compiler makes certain

parts.note: hence means therefore, or so
the setter speaking of themself is me

explanation.surface: The setter claims to make sure of things for that reason.
explanation.definitionFit: In 'certain people' and 'some people' the two words are interchangeable determiners.

clue.text: Will providing us with a rich inheritance

definitions.text: Will providing us with a rich inheritance

parts.words: Will providing us with a rich inheritance
parts.note: a will is a legal document leaving riches; Will is also the first name of the Bard, whose plays are a cultural legacy

explanation.surface: A legacy left in someone's will makes the heirs wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a testament; it is the playwright's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: William, the Bard, left English speakers an enormous literary legacy of plays and poems.

clue.text: What 'Put a sock in it' means? Rubbish!

parts.note: a dictionary defines a verb with 'to', so what a phrase means is set out as 'to ...'
a slangy order to be quiet, the same as the hushing sound sh

explanation.surface: Someone told to shut up retorts that the request is nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue mimics a dictionary entry: the meaning of 'put a sock in it' is 'to sh', written as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosh is informal British slang for nonsense or worthless talk.

clue.text: It may involve the amputation of limbs

definitions.text: It may involve the amputation of limbs

parts.words: It may involve the amputation of limbs
parts.note: limbs here are the branches of a tree, which an arborist lops off, not a patient's arms and legs

explanation.surface: It reads like a description of a grim hospital operation.
explanation.definitionFit: The care and pruning of trees includes cutting away branches, which are a tree's limbs.

clue.text: Tip 'Heyday'

definitions.meaning: a tip is the pointed top of a mountain or similar
a heyday is the time of greatest success, the high point

explanation.definitionFit: Both a mountain's summit and a period of greatest success are described by the same word for a high point.

clue.text: Straight away, how one knew dog had fleas

definitions.meaning: starting at the very beginning, with nothing done beforehand

definitions.text: how one knew dog had fleas
definitions.meaning: a dog's itching and scratching gives away its fleas

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a flea-ridden dog at once.
explanation.definitionFit: To start with no head start is to begin from nothing, right at the outset.

clue.text: Losing a friend with fever and disease

indicators.note: losing means a letter is lost from the following word

parts.note: a pal is a friend
ague is an old word for a malarial fever

explanation.surface: Someone loses a friend to fever and sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: A plague is an epidemic illness, such as the Black Death.

clue.text: Shamefaced, formerly admitted having spilled the beans

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so one piece is let into another

parts.note: someone shamefaced goes red in the face
late means former, as in the late president

explanation.surface: Someone who confessed now blushes about having done so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted' sounds like confessing, which fits the surface, but it signals letting one piece in.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate something is to tell or recount it, as someone who has spilled the beans has done.

clue.text: And I engineered run on foreign currency

indicators.note: engineered means contrived or rebuilt, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of rigging a run on a foreign money market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engineered' turns AND I into DINA.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the unit of money in several countries, such as Kuwait, Jordan and Serbia.

clue.text: Picks out for union potential strikers

definitions.meaning: pairs off, as a matchmaker chooses two people to marry
things that may be struck, as a match is struck to light it

explanation.surface: A union leader picks out workers who might go on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' and 'strikers' suggest a labour dispute; in fact one is marriage and the other is lighting a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A matchmaker pairs off couples, and the small sticks struck to make fire share that word.

clue.text: Say something dumb

parts.note: dumb means silent, so this is forming words with the lips and no sound

explanation.surface: It reads as a call to utter something foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dumb' looks like stupid, but means silent.
explanation.definitionFit: To form words silently with the lips is the verb sense of this body part.

clue.text: They beat Republican in eliminating contests

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside

parts.note: heats are preliminary races that knock out the slower entrants

explanation.surface: A Republican candidate defeats rivals in the primaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They beat' suggests winners; here it is what the organs do.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts are the organs that pump blood with a steady pulse.

clue.text: Yorkshire city gravestone might have it

definitions.meaning: a small cathedral city in North Yorkshire, England
a gravestone might have R.I.P. carved on it

explanation.surface: A city in Yorkshire might have its name carved on a tombstone.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second half as RIP plus ON: a headstone may have 'Rest in peace' on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripon is a cathedral city in North Yorkshire, in northern England.

clue.text: Fools such as these, embracing sin, could result in deep thoughts

definitions.text: such as these, embracing sin, could result in deep thoughts
definitions.meaning: the word wrapped round the letters of sin spells a word for contemplations

explanation.surface: Gullible people who flirt with sin may end up deep in thought.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: put SIN inside the answer and you get MUSINGS, which are deep thoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: Mugs is British slang for gullible people, easily duped dupes or suckers.

clue.text: 'That ain't no lady'? Bad English

parts.note: mal is French for bad, as in the prefix of malpractice

explanation.surface: Someone scolds poor grammar in the double negative of 'That ain't no lady'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad English' looks like a comment on the grammar, but it is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is no lady is a man or a boy, so it belongs to the masculine sex.

clue.text: Irritable with pests

definitions.meaning: infested with rodents, full of rats

explanation.surface: Someone grows irritable when bothered by pests.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is British informal for bad-tempered, and literally describes a place overrun by rodents.

clue.text: Scold for always turning round

indicators.note: round means the reversed word goes round the other piece
turning means the word is read backwards

parts.note: ever means always
pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: Someone is told off for forever turning round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' looks like a link word but supplies letters; 'turning' makes REVE, and 'round' puts it around them.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprove is to rebuke or tell off, a synonym of chide.

clue.text: Some feet and limb that one finds in marina

parts.note: a yard is three feet
an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: Feet and limbs suggest a body part seen at a seaside harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feet' and 'limb' paint a body; they are a unit of length and an arm.
explanation.definitionFit: The spar ends on a sailing ship's mast are found on boats moored where yachts berth.

clue.text: Able to hold a dangerous object?

indicators.note: one piece holds another, so it goes round it

parts.note: an able person is clever

explanation.surface: A question of whether someone is competent to handle something hazardous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold' puts A inside CLEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A butcher's chopper with a heavy blade is an example of something hazardous to handle.

clue.text: Writing with broken heart about pet

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, round, the other piece
a broken heart is in pieces, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Someone writes, heartbroken, about a lost pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken heart' reads as grief, but 'broken' makes HATER and 'about' puts it around the abbreviation for a manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: This small furry rodent is a familiar household pet kept in a cage.

clue.text: As well as hole left to fill

indicators.note: one piece goes into another to fill it

parts.note: taken as written
O is a hole, from its shape

explanation.surface: Instructions to fill a hole that was left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As well as' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'well'; 'to fill' puts L inside AS, then O follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in addition or too, just like the phrase meaning besides.

clue.text: Prevent trophies being lifted

indicators.note: in a down answer, lifting the word means reading it upwards, backwards

parts.note: pots is sporting slang for cups or trophies

explanation.surface: Someone stops a team from raising their cups in triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop something is to hinder or block it from happening.

clue.text: Excitement as it's heading towards north side

indicators.note: in a down answer, going north means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: R is right, one side

explanation.surface: Excitement at a team heading for the north side of a ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading towards north' makes STI from IT'S.
explanation.definitionFit: A stir is a commotion or flurry of excitement.

clue.text: Cracked up in shock

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means reading the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: cracked means crazy, nuts

explanation.surface: Someone cracked up in a state of shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracked up' reads as broke down; it is the synonym and the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to astonish or daze them with a shock.

clue.text: With 'goodbye' over, I dropped drink

indicators.note: dropped means a letter is left out
over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: adios is Spanish for goodbye

explanation.surface: After saying goodbye, someone dropped their drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' makes SOIDA from ADIOS; 'dropped' takes out the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda is fizzy water or a soft drink.

clue.text: Isn't, for instance, to do with drawing

definitions.meaning: a word shortened with an apostrophe, like is not becoming isn't
drawing together or in, as muscles tighten

explanation.surface: It sounds like a grammar point linked to sketching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' suggests sketching, but it means pulling together.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortened form such as isn't is one sense; the act of drawing together or shrinking is the other.

clue.text: My penny or pound

parts.note: my! and coo! are both exclamations of surprise
P is the abbreviation for penny in British money

explanation.surface: It reads as a choice between British coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penny' and 'pound' suggest money, but a pound is an enclosure for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A pound is an enclosure for animals, and a coop is a cage or pen for poultry.

clue.text: Tired out chaps returning belatedly, mostly — it's bad

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: chaps are men

indicators.note: returning means the shortened word is read backwards
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: something done belatedly is done late

explanation.surface: Weary men getting home late is not a good thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns TIRED into DETRI; 'mostly' cuts LATE to LAT, and 'returning' turns that to TAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Detrimental means harmful or damaging, so it describes something that does harm.
